question: 你资料里的 CBT-I 指什么？它在长期失眠治疗中通常处于什么位置？
answer:
CBT-I 是“失眠认知行为治疗”（Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia）的缩写，是一种针对失眠的结构化非药物疗法，而不是单纯“讲道理”的心理咨询。

**它包含什么**
按美国国立心肺血液研究所（NHLBI）的说明，CBT-I 通常持续六到八周，内容包括处理与睡眠相关的想法、放松训练、睡眠教育以及行为技术；可以面对面进行，也可以通过电话或线上方式提供 [H3:CBTI]。其中“刺激控制”是常见的行为成分之一：困了才上床，躺不着就离开床，等有困意再回来，并尽量让床只与睡眠相关 [H3:StimulusControl]。CBT-I 里还常包含睡眠限制成分，但这部分需要由专业人员根据个人情况调整，不适合自己随意压缩卧床时间 [H3:CBTI]。

**在长期失眠治疗中的位置**
NHLBI 把 CBT-I 描述为长期失眠“通常的首选治疗”（usual first treatment），也就是说在治疗顺序上它一般排在药物之前 [H3:CBTI]。这里的“长期失眠”指持续较久、而非偶发几晚的睡眠困难；NHS 以三个月作为区分短期困难与长期失眠的时间界线，但单凭时长本身并不能确立诊断 [H4:WhenToSeekHelp]。

**什么时候值得寻求专业评估**
如果睡眠困难已持续数月、自己调整习惯没有改善，或已经明显影响日常生活，NHS 建议进行临床评估 [H4:WhenToSeekHelp]。具体是否适合 CBT-I、如何安排疗程，需要由专业人员判断；我这里只能介绍一般资料，不能替代诊断或制定个人治疗方案。

retrieved_evidence.title: NIH/NHLBI · Insomnia Treatment
retrieved_evidence.scope: Insomnia treatment education; no individualized prescription
retrieved_evidence.text: NHLBI describes cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), commonly delivered over six to eight weeks, as the usual first treatment for long-term insomnia. It includes work on sleep-related thoughts, relaxation, education and behavioral techniques. Support can be in person, by phone or online. Do not turn its sleep-restriction component into a self-prescribed reduced sleep window; clinician-guided tailoring matters.

retrieved_evidence.title: NIH/NHLBI · Insomnia Treatment
retrieved_evidence.scope: Insomnia treatment education; no individualized prescription
retrieved_evidence.text: Stimulus control links bed with sleep: go to bed when sleepy, leave bed if unable to sleep, and return when sleepy. Use bed for sleep rather than prolonged wakeful activities. This is one component of CBT-I, not proof of a diagnosis.

retrieved_evidence.title: NHS · Insomnia
retrieved_evidence.text: For difficulty sleeping, keep a regular getting-up time, go to bed when sleepy and allow a relaxing hour before bed. A dark, quiet, comfortable bedroom can help. After a poor night, avoid sleeping in to compensate. For insomnia, NHS advises avoiding daytime naps; this is more restrictive than general short-nap guidance and should not be presented as a universal ban for every sleeper.

retrieved_evidence.title: NHS · Insomnia
retrieved_evidence.text: Seek a clinical review if sleep difficulties persist for months, changing habits has not helped, or the problem makes daily life hard to manage. NHS distinguishes short-term difficulties from long-term insomnia at three months; duration alone does not establish a diagnosis. Do not drive when sleepy.
